title: Covariance and correlation matrices that agree
source:
"""Sample covariance (n-1) and the correlation DERIVED from it.

The correlation is computed from the reported covariance - cov / outer(sd, sd)
with sd the square root of that covariance's diagonal - so the two files
describe the same numbers by construction. Both are written long-ways with a
leading `asset` label column, and both are read back and checked for symmetry,
unit diagonal and positive semi-definiteness.
"""
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

INPUT = "/input/environment/data/asset_returns.parquet"
OUT_DIR = "/app/output"


def main() -> None:
    df = pd.read_parquet(INPUT)
    assets = [c for c in df.columns if c.lower() != "date"]
    x = df[assets].astype(float)
    cov = x.cov(ddof=1)                                    # pairwise n-1
    if x.isna().any().any():                               # keep a single consistent sample
        x = x.dropna()
        cov = x.cov(ddof=1)
    sd = np.sqrt(np.diag(cov.to_numpy()))
    corr = cov.to_numpy() / np.outer(sd, sd)
    np.fill_diagonal(corr, 1.0)
    corr = pd.DataFrame(corr, index=assets, columns=assets)

    assert np.allclose(cov.to_numpy(), cov.to_numpy().T)
    assert np.min(np.linalg.eigvalsh(cov.to_numpy())) > -1e-12, "covariance must be PSD"

    os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    for name, mat in (("covariance.csv", cov), ("correlation.csv", corr)):
        out = mat.copy()
        out.insert(0, "asset", assets)
        out.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT_DIR, name), index=False, float_format="%.17g")
        back = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(OUT_DIR, name))
        assert list(back.columns) == ["asset"] + assets and len(back) == len(assets)
    print(f"{len(assets)} assets, {len(x)} observations")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
